notes: Coders agreed on all three documents (university layer, stance delegates) and on unit alignment (68 of 72 A units matched). Main disagreements: (1) actor on informs statements and phase on general advice, resolved from who the page addresses (faculty guidance page: instructor; student page: student) and the phase definitions (general for facts and reflective questions, not before-course); (2) modality of optional assignment-design ideas (may vs should), resolved to may for 'ideas'/'try' wording and should for 'recommend'; (3) unit_stance for disclosure, licensed-tool and procedural statements (permit/restrict vs neutral), resolved by whether the sentence itself permits or limits use; (4) policy_type on borderline units (instructor tool evaluation to P63, tool-terms and platform-policy checks to P50 with fit notes, contract fact to P65, conditional skill-building ban to P19), with the other coder's UNCOVERED or fit notes preserved; (5) coder A merged two assignment ideas into one unit, split per the no-merge rule. 13 single-coder units (4 A, 9 B) were all real statements and kept. Two UNCOVERED units remain (employer rules for applications; choosing a tool designed for the task).
